source: MIT 6.006 Introduction to Algorithms, Lecture 1, ~6-13 min
keypoints: 6.006 covers classic data structures (Python dictionaries, balanced binary search trees) and augments them for efficiency on certain problems.
The follow-on course for much more algorithm design is 6.046 Design and Analysis of Algorithms.
6.006 involves some design but a whole lot of analysis of algorithms.
Students do real implementations of the data structures and algorithms in Python.
Each problem set has both a theory part and a programming part.
The course has eight modules, each roughly with an associated problem set.
The first module is algorithmic thinking, kick-started with the peak-finding problem.
In the first problem set, some provided Python algorithms contain bugs; students analyze their complexity, identify which are correct and efficient, and write a proof for one.
The second problem set is simulating a logic network using a particular sorting algorithm and data structure.
The hashing module includes genome comparison; human and rat genomes were found to be 99% similar.
If an algorithm's complexity is too high, the program will not finish on the large inputs used in problem sets.
By 'fun' problem sets the instructor means challenging and worthwhile, not easy.
